title: #theatre #aliashawkat #arresteddevelopment #nyc
transcript: when I heard that Alia Shawkat from Arrested Development was gonna star alongside some of the best actors in New York in a Clare Barron play I almost lost my mind and thankfully it was everything I hoped for and more. if I described the plot of this play to you about a woman who returns to her childhood home to take care of her sick father it would probably sound like every family drama that's ever been written but it's simply not not only does the play nail its sort of dry, understated humor and its relatable emotions what really set this play apart for me is that it's so meticulously textured with all these little details in the way these characters behave and interact with each other details that in the hands of different artists might have come across contrived or distracting but here just felt so sharp and achingly human there's this moment where she's like on top of the bed and she's looking for something underneath the bed but she can't find it so in her feeling of defeat she kinda just hangs limply upside down for the next several minutes of the scene and it's one of those moments that you wouldn't normally think to write and yet it's like “yeah, we've all been there!” there is a lot of organic laugh out loud humor in the play but it also has this pretty quiet, hyper-naturalistic feel to it which is difficult to do as well as they do it here and even still it might not be everyone's cup of tea but for me it was one of those theatrical experiences where I was so deeply absorbed in every scene and just like the little interactions between these characters who felt so real to me that it almost didn't occur to me to consider what the play was even about thematically but in retrospect, and as the title suggests, I think it's about that awkward cognitive dissonance of you and your parents both being adults at the same time and kind of dancing around that question of: who's taking care of who? and this whole cast honestly Alia Shawkat is great Peter Friedman and Caleb Eberhardt are literally two of my favorite actors seeing them in the same play kinda blew my mind so You Got Older is currently running at the Cherry Lane through April 12th and heads up, they do have a $40 rush if the full price is a little too steep for you
classificationReason: Creator reviews a Clare Barron play starring Alia Shawkat about a woman returning home to care for her sick father — matching You Got Older. They attended and share detailed first-hand opinions on the writing, humor, performances, and specific staging moments.
